newsitem.title: GERMANY: Every second German ready to cheat on tax - study.
newsitem.headline: Every second German ready to cheat on tax - study.

text.p: One in two Germans would be prepared under certain circumstances to cheat the taxman, the German Federation of Taxpayers said, presenting a survey on Tuesday.

A third of those polled said they would dodge tax if they knew that any possible fine if caught would not exceed the profit to be had from the evasion. That proportion declined as the size of the potential fine rose.

Just 30 percent thought that holding back income gained from second jobs was a serious offence, while a mere 20 percent disapproved strongly of scams to avoid paying value-added tax, the survey found.
A huge 85 percent of those polled said they thought the German tax system was unfair, and more than the two-thirds thought they had to pay too much tax.

The survey comes amid Bonn's continued failure to push through a tax reform originally intended to slash 30 billion marks ($16.4 billion) from the nation's tax bill, at the same time closing dozens of tax loopholes.

The Spiegel news weekly reported at the weekend that the government was now working on a revenue-neutral measure in a bid to get support from the rival Social Democrats (SPD), who can block the reform in parliament.
Just under a half of those surveyed believed the initial tax reform had foundered as a deliberate result of political tactics by Germany's major parties ahead of the September 1998 general elections.

A summary copy of the survey, carried out for the taxpayers' federation by the Research Unit for Empirical Social-Economy in Cologne, did not say how many people had been questioned. ($ = 1.834 German Marks)
